adjudication_records.issue_text: `totalPages` computed property in admin-group.js.es6 uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 instead of Math.ceil(user_count / limit), causing an off-by-one phantom empty page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit

Stale offset after removing the last member of a final partial page: neither the client (findMembers clamping) nor the server (groups_controller.rb members) adjusts offset when user_count shrinks to a multiple of limit at or below the current offset, resulting in a blank member list

Public group members page is silently truncated to 50 members: the server hard-caps at limit 50 and the public members route fetches once with no pagination UI in members.hbs, so end users can never see more than 50 members

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always apply `limit`/`offset` with a default `limit = 50` for *all* groups (previously only automatic groups were limited; others returned the full list). On the client, `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6` now calls `model.findMembers()` once and the template `group/members.hbs` iterates `{{#each m in members}}` with no pagination controls or actions, so a user viewing the public group members page will only ever see the first page of results (50 by default). The proposed finding is slightly imprecise in saying the server "hard-caps" at 50 (it accepts a `limit` param), but the effective UX regression—no way to see beyond the first 50 from the UI—is verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members in admin/groups_controller.rb silently skips nonexistent usernames (User.find_by_username returns nil) and still returns success_json, masking failures as success with no error feedback

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, it iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only calls `group.add(user)` when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user. If a username doesn’t exist, it is simply skipped (no error collected). The action then returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, even if zero (or fewer than requested) members were actually added. This matches the finding: nonexistent usernames are silently ignored and the response indicates success with no feedback about invalid entries.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Remove link rendered for automatic groups in group_member.hbs because the `automatic` property resolves against the member (Discourse.User) instead of the group controller, offering a removeMember action that always fails with 422
findMembers in group.js returns undefined instead of a promise when the group has no name (previously returned Ember.RSVP.resolve([])), breaking the old contract for callers chaining .then()
matched_golden_ids: Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments point out that certain code paths in the function do not explicitly return a value, causing the function to return undefined (candidate specifies the 'group has no name' branch and the resulting broken promise contract).

adjudication_records.issue_text: usernames.split(",") in admin/groups_controller.rb add_members raises NoMethodError (500) if the usernames param is sent as an array, e.g. by an API client using usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code does `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and then unconditionally calls `usernames.split(",")`. If an API client submits `usernames` as an array (e.g. `usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b`), Rails will populate `params[:usernames]` as an Array, and Array does not implement `split`, causing a NoMethodError and a 500. The diff contains no normalization/guard (e.g. `Array(usernames).join(',')`), so this is a real defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addMembers/removeMember in group.js only handle the success path with no .catch or error handling, so 422 responses or network failures are silently dropped with no feedback shown to the admin

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `addMembers` and `removeMember` in `group.js` do `Discourse.ajax(...).then(() => self.findMembers())` with no local rejection handler, and the controller actions call these methods without chaining `.then/.catch`. However, the finding’s key claim that 422s/network failures are "silently dropped with no feedback" is not verifiable from the diff alone because `Discourse.ajax` may have global error handling/notifications elsewhere in the codebase. The diff only proves lack of local handling, not that the admin sees no feedback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The first remove_member controller spec uses xhr :put instead of exercising the actual DELETE route, providing false routing coverage since controller specs dispatch the action regardless of verb
Removal of PATCH /admin/groups/:id (incremental changes) and group[usernames] in PUT /admin/groups/:id is a breaking API change for external consumers that should be flagged in release notes

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the previous incremental membership update behavior via PATCH in `Admin::GroupsController#update` (the `update_patch` method and `request.patch?` branching are deleted) and removes support for `params[:group][:usernames]` / nested `params[:group]` payloads in both `create` and `update` (now reads top-level `params[:name]`, `params[:visible]`, `params[:alias_level]`). Membership changes are moved to new endpoints `PUT /admin/groups/:group_id/members` and `DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members`. The controller spec also deletes the incremental PATCH tests, confirming the old API is no longer supported. External consumers relying on PATCH `changes` or PUT with `group[usernames]` would break, so this is a verifiable breaking API change introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The usernames input is not cleared after addMembers, so a second click of 'Add' re-submits the same users

adjudication.rationale: In the new `addMembers` action in `admin-group.js.es6`, the code submits `this.get("usernames")` to `model.addMembers(...)` but never resets/clears the `usernames` property afterward. The template includes an explicit Add button (`{{action "addMembers"}}`), so clicking it a second time will re-submit the same usernames still in the input. The inline comment `// TODO: should clear the input` also confirms this behavior is currently unimplemented.

adjudication_records.issue_text: N+1 query shape in add_members: per-username User.find_by_username lookups and per-member individual INSERTs instead of a bulk User.where(username_lower: [...]) fetch plus bulk insert

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` (added in this diff), the code does `usernames.split(",").each` and for each username performs `User.find_by_username(username)`, which is one DB query per username. It then calls `group.add(user)` per found user, which typically results in one membership insert per user as well. This is a classic N-per-item query/insert pattern that could be replaced with a single `User.where(username_lower: ...)` (or similar) fetch and bulk association creation. The issue is directly visible and verifiable from the diff as a potential performance defect for large username lists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members operation is non-transactional, regressing from the previous atomic validation via group.save on a usernames= assignment

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `add_members` controller action that loops over `usernames.split(",")` and calls `group.add(user)` for each found user, then calls `group.save`. While this *could* be non-transactional depending on how `Group#add` is implemented (e.g., if it writes join rows immediately), the proposed finding specifically claims a regression from “previous atomic validation via `group.save` on a `usernames=` assignment”. That prior atomic/transactional behavior is not verifiable from this diff because the implementation of `Group#usernames=` (and whether it was transactional) is not shown here. Both old and new flows call `group.save` after mutating membership, and nothing in the diff demonstrates that the old approach was atomic while the new one is not. Therefore the finding relies on speculation beyond the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded client-controlled limit and offset on the public group members endpoint: limit is not clamped to a maximum and offset is not clamped to >= 0, allowing clients to defeat pagination and trigger unbounded queries/materialization (and a negative offset causes a 500)

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff changes pagination to accept `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i`, then directly applies them to `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`. There is no clamping of `limit` to a reasonable maximum (client can request an arbitrarily large limit, potentially forcing very large result sets/materialization), and no clamping of `offset` to >= 0 (a client can send a negative offset, which Rails/ActiveRecord may reject/raise and return a 500). Previously, the code effectively bounded automatic-group pagination with a default/max-like behavior (200) and only applied limit/offset in that case; the new code exposes unbounded, client-controlled values for all groups.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No bound on the size of the usernames payload in add_members, allowing a single request to carry tens of thousands of usernames and making the N+1 cost unbounded

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the diff shows `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` followed by `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` and for each element it does `User.find_by_username(username)` and `group.add(user)`. There is no limit/validation on how many usernames can be supplied, and the per-username lookup is an explicit N-per-user query pattern. A single large `usernames` string can therefore drive an unbounded number of DB lookups and membership operations in one request (even if restricted to admins), making request cost unbounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New COUNT(*) on group.users.count runs on every members request, a per-request full count over the group membership join on a hot public route instead of using a cheaper source like a counter cache

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff introduces `total = group.users.count` and returns it in `meta.total` for every members request. That adds an extra COUNT query per request (likely `COUNT(*)` over the group membership association/join). Previously the action did not compute a total count at all, and the Group model/serializers already expose `user_count`, suggesting a cheaper cached value may exist. This is a verifiable per-request performance regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers clamps offset using possibly-stale user_count before the request, causing wrong computed offsets in findMembers and admin-group next/previous actions, leading to wasted duplicate fetches and wrong-page UX

Breaking response-shape change on public GET /groups/:group_id/members: previously returned a bare serialized array, now returns { members: [...], meta: { total, limit, offset } }, breaking external consumers that map over the array, with no versioning or deprecation path

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` (public GET `/groups/:group_id/members`) from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)`—which would return a bare JSON array of serialized members—to `render json: { members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }`, i.e., an object wrapper with pagination metadata. This is a concrete, observable response-shape change in the diff and would break any existing consumers expecting the endpoint to return an array they can directly iterate/map over. There is no versioning, alternate endpoint, or backward-compatible root key shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pagination defaults changed on GET /groups/:group_id/members: non-automatic groups previously returned all members unpaginated and automatic groups defaulted to limit=200, both now default to limit=50, silently truncating results

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the old behavior returned *all* members for non-automatic groups (no `limit/offset` applied) and only applied pagination to automatic groups with a default `limit` of 200. The diff changes this to always apply `limit`/`offset` for all groups, with `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i`, meaning requests that don’t pass `limit` will now only return 50 members. This is a verifiable behavior/API change that can truncate results for existing consumers that expected the full list by default.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public group members page is silently truncated to 50 members with no pagination controls added to the members template (unlike the admin template which got next/previous actions), a functional regression for large groups

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always apply `limit = (params[:limit] || 50)` and `offset`, returning only a page of members plus `meta.total`. On the public members route (`discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6`), it now sets the controller `model` to the group and calls `model.findMembers()`, which requests members with the group’s default `limit: 50, offset: 0` (`discourse/models/group.js`). The public template (`discourse/templates/group/members.hbs`) was updated to iterate `{{#each m in members}}`, but no pagination controls/actions were added there (unlike the admin template which added next/previous actions). As a result, the public members page will only ever show the first 50 members with no way in this diff to navigate to subsequent pages, which is a functional regression for large groups.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Route param mismatch on new member endpoints: routes defined as member routes inside resources :groups populate params[:id], but add_members/remove_member in admin/groups_controller.rb use params.require(:group_id), likely causing ActionController::ParameterMissing (400) and breaking the whole feature
Controller specs for add_members/remove_member pass group_id explicitly, bypassing routing entirely, so the suite cannot catch the group_id vs :id param mismatch

Admin API contract break: create and update in admin/groups_controller.rb now read flat params (params[:name], params[:visible], params[:alias_level]) instead of nested group[...] params, breaking external API consumers that POST {group: {name: ...}}

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows Admin::GroupsController#create and #update no longer read nested params (previously params[:group][:name], params[:group][:visible], etc.) and instead read flat params (params[:name], params[:visible], params[:alias_level]). There is no fallback handling for the old { group: { ... } } shape, and the specs were updated to send flat params, confirming the intentional change. Any external client still POSTing/PUTting the old nested payload would now fail to create/update correctly (e.g., name becomes '' in create), which is an API contract break relative to the prior behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removed PATCH membership API (update_patch handling params[:changes][:add]/[:delete]) and PUT group[usernames] full-replacement logic, but PATCH and PUT still route to update and return success_json while silently no-oping membership changes

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::GroupsController#update` was rewritten to only handle `alias_level`, `visible`, and (non-automatic) `name`. The prior logic that applied membership changes via PATCH (`params[:changes][:add]/[:delete]`) and via PUT (`params[:group][:usernames]`) was removed. However, Rails’ standard `resources :groups` routing still maps both PATCH and PUT `/admin/groups/:id` to `update` (no route change removing those verbs). As a result, clients sending the old membership params will get a normal `success_json` response (assuming `group.save` succeeds) but the membership params are ignored, i.e., membership updates become a silent no-op.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pagination off-by-one in totalPages computed in admin-group.js.es6: Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 overcounts when user_count is a multiple of limit, causing navigation to an empty page and showLast never being true on the real last page so the next arrow is never disabled

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` (when `user_count != 0`). If `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 50 users, limit 50), this yields 2 pages instead of 1. `next` then sets `offset` to `Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)` which becomes `user_count` (e.g., 50), and `Group.findMembers()` requests `offset=50`, producing an empty member list page. Also, `showingLast` (propertyEqual currentPage/totalPages) will be false on the real last page and only true on the empty extra page, so the next arrow isn’t disabled when it should be.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public JS model API changed without caller consideration: findMembers() now resolves to the raw AJAX response object ({members, meta}) instead of an array of Discourse.User, and saveWithUsernames()/createWithUsernames() were removed outright, breaking plugin callers

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change the JS API: `Group.findMembers()` no longer returns an array of `Discourse.User` like before. However, it also does **not** “resolve to the raw AJAX response object”; the `.then(...)` callback only calls `self.setProperties(...)` and returns nothing, so the promise resolves to `undefined` while populating `group.members` as a side effect. All call sites shown in the diff were updated to stop depending on the return value (they just call `model.findMembers()`), so there’s no verifiable breakage within this change set. The removal of `saveWithUsernames()` / `createWithUsernames()` is real, but claiming it breaks plugin callers is speculative and not verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Spec for remove_member uses the wrong HTTP verb (xhr :put instead of xhr :delete matching the route definition), reducing test fidelity since controller specs bypass routing
matched_golden_ids: The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that the remove_member spec uses xhr :put but the route expects a DELETE request (xhr :delete), causing a mismatch in HTTP verb and reduced test fidelity.

adjudication_records.issue_text: totalPages calculation uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 which produces a phantom empty last page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, enabling 'next' navigation to an empty page
matched_golden_ids: The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same pagination bug: using Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1 yields an extra (phantom) page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, allowing navigation to an empty page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers offset clamp uses Math.min(user_count, ...) instead of (totalPages-1)*limit, perpetuating the off-by-one pagination error
matched_golden_ids: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments describe the same pagination off-by-one: clamping the next offset to user_count/total can yield offset == total (rather than the start of the last page), producing an empty final page. The candidate frames it as using Math.min(user_count, ...) instead of (totalPages-1)*limit, which is the same underlying bug and UX issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: After removing the last member of a page, the stale offset is not backed up to the previous page, causing findMembers to return an empty member list

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Discourse.Group#removeMember`, after the DELETE it simply calls `self.findMembers()` without adjusting `offset`. `findMembers()` clamps the request offset using the *current* `this.get("user_count")` (which is stale until the response returns), and the server (`GroupsController#members`) uses the provided `offset` directly (no bounding). If you delete the last member on the last page such that the new total makes the current `offset` >= new total (e.g., total 51/limit 50/offset 50 -> delete one -> total 50), the subsequent request still uses offset 50 and the server returns an empty `members` array, leaving the UI on an empty page instead of backing up to the previous page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server-side add_members silently skips unknown usernames and still renders success_json, giving admins no error feedback for typos

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only adds users when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user; unknown usernames are simply skipped. It then renders `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, with no reporting of skipped/invalid usernames. However, this same “silent success on unknown usernames” behavior existed in the prior incremental update path (and was explicitly tested), so it’s not a clear newly introduced defect or objectively incorrect behavior in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-side addMembers fires AJAX with no .then/.catch handling and never clears the input, so failed add attempts provide no feedback and re-submitting repeats the silent failure

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `addMembers` in `admin-group.js.es6` calling `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` without returning the promise and with a `// TODO: should clear the input` comment, so the input is indeed not cleared. However, the finding’s main claim that failures are “silent” and provide “no feedback” is not verifiable from this diff: `Discourse.ajax` may have global error handling elsewhere, and nothing in the diff demonstrates that a failed request produces no UI feedback. The “re-submitting repeats the silent failure” part is also speculative beyond what’s shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member can raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound (unhandled 500) when the user_id is not currently a member, due to has_many :through delete with no pre-check

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the code does `group.users.delete(user_id)`. This will remove the join-row(s) for that user id if present, and if the user is not currently a member it typically results in deleting 0 join rows (no-op) rather than raising `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound`. The diff does not show any `find` scoped to the association membership (e.g., `group.users.find(user_id)`) that would fail when the user isn’t a member. While some Rails versions may raise if the *User record itself* doesn’t exist (because `delete` with an integer id can internally `User.find(id)`), that is different from “not currently a member”. So the finding, as stated, is not a verifiable problem in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member renders success_json unconditionally, reporting success even when the removal did nothing

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `remove_member` does **not** render `success_json` unconditionally: it calls `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then `if group.save` renders success, else renders `render_json_error(group)`. While it may still return success when `delete` is a no-op (e.g., user not in group), that behavior is consistent with idempotent “remove” semantics and is not shown to be incorrect by the diff. The finding’s claim of unconditional success is a misread of the code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Routes changed from returning the members promise in afterModel to fire-and-forget findMembers() in setupController, so member-fetch errors are swallowed and the UI silently renders '0 members' with no error state
matched_golden_ids: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same underlying problem: findMembers() is invoked asynchronously in a fire-and-forget way (no awaiting/returning), so the controller/route can render before member data arrives. The candidate additionally notes swallowed errors and silent '0 members' rendering, which are consequences of the unhandled async call/race condition described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers returns undefined instead of Ember.RSVP.resolve([]) when name is empty, which will throw for any future caller that chains .then()

adjudication.rationale: In discourse/models/group.js, findMembers was changed from returning `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])` when `name` is empty to `return ;` (i.e., returning `undefined`). That makes the method’s return type inconsistent: it usually returns the `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` promise, but returns `undefined` for an empty name. Any caller that previously (or later) does `group.findMembers().then(...)` will throw because `.then` is called on `undefined`. This is a concrete behavioral regression from the prior implementation shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public members endpoint accepts unbounded limit (e.g. limit=1000000) that can serialize the entire user table, and unvalidated values allow arbitrary limits on public endpoints

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` is used directly in `group.users...limit(limit)` with no upper bound/clamp. A client can request `?limit=1000000` and force the server to load/serialize an extremely large member list. While it’s scoped to `group.users` (not an unconstrained `User` query), some groups (e.g., an “everyone”/very large group) can effectively cover most/all users, so the endpoint can be abused to serialize a huge portion of the user table. The diff introduces pagination defaults but still leaves the limit unvalidated/unbounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public members endpoint accepts unvalidated negative offset which produces invalid SQL on Postgres, causing a 500

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then calls `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no clamping/validation. If a client supplies `offset=-1` (or any negative), ActiveRecord will generate `OFFSET -1`, which PostgreSQL rejects (“OFFSET must not be negative”), resulting in a 500. This is a concrete behavior introduced by the new pagination logic for all groups.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No guard against concurrent/out-of-order member fetches: pagination buttons aren't disabled while fetching and there's no request sequencing, so rapid clicks can leave displayed list and pagination state inconsistent

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `next`/`previous` actions immediately mutate `group.offset` and then call `group.findMembers()`, which performs an async `Discourse.ajax(...)` and, on completion, blindly `setProperties({ user_count, limit, offset, members })` from that response. There is no loading flag to disable pagination controls and no request sequencing/cancellation, so multiple rapid clicks can create multiple in-flight requests; if an earlier request resolves after a later one, it will overwrite `members` and `offset` with stale data (from `result.meta.offset`), making the displayed list/pagination state inconsistent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Spec exercises remove_member with xhr :put while the route is wired as DELETE, and controller specs bypass routing, so the test passes despite the verb mismatch and cannot catch routing regressions

adjudication.rationale: In config/routes.rb the admin groups member-removal endpoint is defined as `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`, so the correct HTTP verb is DELETE. However, in `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` the new `.remove_member` context invokes the action with `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...` (visible in the diff). Controller specs call the controller action directly and do not validate that a matching route exists for that verb/path, so this test can pass even if the routing is wrong and will not catch regressions/mismatches between the intended DELETE route and the exercised PUT request.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Controller reads params.require(:group_id) but member routes under resources :groups supply the id as params[:id], so every real request to add_members/remove_member raises ActionController::ParameterMissing
matched_golden_ids: The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same bug: the routes provide the group's identifier as params[:id], but the controller/action is trying to fetch it from params[:group_id] (via require), which fails and breaks the group membership actions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Controller specs call actions directly with hand-fed group_id, bypassing routing and masking the route param-name mismatch; a request or routing spec would have caught it

groups#members response format changed from serialized array to {members: [...], meta: {total, limit, offset}} with no test coverage for the new shape, limit/offset handling, or edge cases like missing/zero/negative offset
New frontend pagination logic untested and totalPages = floor(user_count / limit) + 1 has an off-by-one producing an extra empty page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1` (except when `user_count == 0`). This is off-by-one when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 100/50 => floor(2)+1 = 3, but there are only 2 pages). The correct logic would be `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (with 0 handled separately). This can make `showingLast` false on the true last page and allow navigating to an extra empty page. The “untested” part is not verifiable from the diff alone, but the off-by-one bug is.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Deleted regression tests for updating non-automatic group's name/alias_level/visible were not replaced; the new suite only tests the automatic-group case

adjudication.rationale: In spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb, the previous `.update` context tested updating a non-automatic group (changing name and setting usernames) and also had incremental PATCH add/delete membership tests. In the new diff, the `.update` context only contains a single test: "ignore name change on automatic group" (id: 1), and there are no replacement tests covering updating a normal (non-automatic) group’s name, alias_level, or visible. Thus the finding that regression coverage for non-automatic updates was removed and not replaced is directly verifiable in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Deleted tests for silent-ignore of non-existent users on add and non-members on remove were not replaced; nothing pins down the silent-ignore behavior of the new add_members

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the previous controller spec coverage that asserted “succeeds silently when adding non-existent users” and “succeeds silently when removing non-members” (the whole incremental PATCH update context was deleted). The new specs add tests for adding several members and for blocking automatic groups, but they do not add any replacement assertion that add_members ignores unknown usernames (or that remove_member ignores non-members). The new implementation of add_members does still silently ignore unknown users via `if user = User.find_by_username(username) ... end`, but there is indeed no test pinning that behavior down anymore.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member error path is dead code: group.users.delete(user_id) executes the delete immediately so the subsequent group.save won't populate errors and render_json_error(group) is unreachable; removing a non-member is untested

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the code calls `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then branches on `if group.save ... else render_json_error(group)`. The association delete performs the removal immediately (it issues the join-table delete and does not depend on `group.save`). Therefore `group.save` is not actually validating/committing the membership removal, and the “error” branch does not reflect failure of the removal. Worse, if `group.save` were to fail for unrelated validation reasons, the controller would return an error even though the member has already been removed (no transaction/rollback). This makes the error-handling path effectively meaningless for the operation being performed, and the behavior for deleting a non-member isn’t covered by tests in the shown spec changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No end-to-end or request-level test for the new create-then-add-members flow (create/save no longer accept usernames, only PUT members), which demonstrably fails through real routes

Pagination/view state (limit, offset, user_count, cached members array) now lives on the shared Group model, leaking transient admin-UI session state to all consumers of Group, where two screens can clobber each other's offset

Pagination math is computed in three places with three sources of truth (controller computeds, controller next/previous actions, model findMembers re-clamping, plus server meta), allowing them to disagree

totalPages off-by-one: Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 returns an extra page when user_count is exactly divisible by limit (100 users / 50 per page shows 3 pages and 'next' navigates to an empty page); should be Math.floor((user_count - 1) / limit) + 1

adjudication.rationale: In admin-group.js.es6, totalPages is computed as Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1 when user_count > 0. If user_count is exactly divisible by limit (e.g., 100/50), this yields 3 pages instead of 2. The next action uses offset = Math.min(offset + limit, user_count), so from page 2 (offset 50) it advances to offset 100, and Group.findMembers() requests /members.json with offset=100 which returns an empty members list (server uses limit/offset directly). This creates an extra empty page and matches the finding’s off-by-one description.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers has an inconsistent return contract: returns undefined when group name is empty but a Promise otherwise, breaking any caller that chains .then()

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js`, `findMembers` was changed from always returning a Promise (`Ember.RSVP.resolve([])` when `name` is empty) to returning `undefined` when `name` is empty: `if (Em.isEmpty(this.get('name'))) { return ; }`. Otherwise it returns the `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` Promise. That creates an inconsistent return contract and would indeed break any caller that does `group.findMembers().then(...)` in the empty-name case (calling `.then` on `undefined`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Membership business logic moved into the Rails controller (add_members/remove_member reimplementing User.find_by_username and group.add), duplicating the Group model's existing usernames= setter and creating two code paths with divergent semantics
add_members silently skips unknown usernames with no error, so the admin gets a 'success' message for a typo'd user with no feedback

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, usernames are split and each is looked up with User.find_by_username. Unknown usernames are simply skipped because the code only does `group.add(user)` inside `if user = ...` and has no else branch to record or report failures. The action then renders `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, which will typically succeed even if zero users were added. This means a typo’d/unknown username yields a successful response with no feedback about the skipped entry, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers addresses the group by mutable user-editable name instead of id, causing 404s or wrong-group fetches after a rename

adjudication.rationale: In `Discourse.Group#findMembers` the URL is built from `this.get('name')` (`/groups/` + name + `/members.json`). In the admin template, non-automatic groups bind the editable name field directly to `model.name` (`{{text-field ... value=name}}`). That means as soon as an admin types a new name (before saving), subsequent member reloads/pagination/removal-triggered reloads call `findMembers()` using the unsaved, potentially non-existent name, which can yield 404s (or fetch a different group if a name collision were possible). This is a concrete correctness risk created by combining a mutable client-side `name` with member fetches keyed by that name rather than an immutable id.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New CSS bundles .groups and .badges under one selector, so changes to badges form styling silently restyle groups and vice versa

adjudication.rationale: The diff intentionally introduces a shared SCSS block `.groups, .badges { .form-horizontal { ... } }` to apply the same baseline form styling to both sections, and simultaneously removes the duplicated rules from `section.details .form-horizontal`. While this does couple future styling changes between groups and badges, the diff does not show any incorrect behavior, regression, or conflicting requirements between the two. The finding is therefore a speculative maintainability concern rather than a verifiable defect introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New .groups CSS overrides the user-selector component's internal styles from outside using !important (width, margin-right, .next/.previous color), leaking across the component boundary

adjudication.rationale:
The added CSS is scoped under `.groups` (and `.groups, .badges`) in `admin_base.scss`. The `!important` rules target `.groups .ac-wrap` and `.groups .ac-wrap .item`, which correspond to the newly added member list wrapper in `admin/templates/group.hbs` (`
{{each member ...}}
`), not clearly the `user-selector` component. The `.next/.previous` rules similarly style the new pagination links in the same template. While this does reach into nested elements and uses `!important`, the diff doesn’t provide evidence that it breaks `user-selector` or “leaks” beyond the `.groups` area; it appears intentional styling for the groups page rather than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The .groups CSS block is placed under the '// Customise area' comment, misleading future readers about its scope

adjudication.rationale: In `admin_base.scss`, the new `.groups` styles are introduced under an explicit `// Groups area` comment and appear *before* the existing `// Customise area` comment. The diff does not show a `.groups` block placed under `// Customise area`, so the finding is not verifiable from the changes and is essentially a comment/style nit rather than a defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicated fire-and-forget member loading (model.findMembers() with no rejection handling) in both admin_group_route setupController and group-members route, swallowing failures and leaving the UI silently empty on network errors

adjudication.rationale:
The diff changes both `admin_group_route.js` and `group-members.js.es6` from returning a promise in `afterModel` (which Ember can use to trigger the route’s error handling when the promise rejects) to calling `model.findMembers()` inside `setupController` without returning/awaiting it and without any `.catch`/rejection handling.

- `app/assets/javascripts/admin/routes/admin_group_route.js`: `setupController` now does `model.findMembers();` and does not return the promise.
- `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6`: `setupController` now does `model.findMembers();` and does not return the promise.

Since `findMembers()` performs `Discourse.ajax(...)` and returns its promise, any network error will reject that promise, but the route will not transition into an error state (unlike when `afterModel` returned the promise). This can leave `members` unset/empty with no explicit handling, i.e., a silent failure from the route’s perspective. The “duplicated” aspect (same pattern in both routes) is verifiable too, though duplication itself isn’t the core defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hardcoded pagination default limit: 50 duplicated across client (group.js) and server (groups_controller.rb), allowing the page display to drift when one changes

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a default `limit: 50` on the client (`Discourse.Group` in group.js) and a server-side fallback `limit = (params[:limit] || 50)` in `GroupsController#members`. However, this is not a verifiable correctness defect from the diff: the client always sends `limit` in `findMembers()` (`data: { limit: this.get("limit"), offset: ... }`), and the client then overwrites its own `limit` from `result.meta.limit` after the request. So even if one side changed, the server-provided meta would keep the client in sync after the first load. The finding describes a potential maintainability concern/speculation about future drift, not a concrete bug introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Spec 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' uses xhr :put, remove_member but the route is delete, so the test doesn't actually exercise remove_member; it should use xhr :delete

adjudication.rationale: In config/routes.rb, the admin group member removal endpoint is defined as `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` (i.e., it expects an HTTP DELETE). However, in `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` under `context ".remove_member"`, the example `"cannot remove members from automatic groups"` calls `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...`, which will not hit the DELETE route and therefore won’t actually exercise `remove_member` as intended. It should use `xhr :delete` to match the route.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Group-member view hardcodes the admin template name (templateName: 'admin/templates/group_member') and adds a classNames 'item' solely to satisfy the admin screen's CSS, leaking admin styling concerns into a generic-sounding view

adjudication.rationale: The new view is defined in `app/assets/javascripts/admin/views/group-member.js.es6`, i.e. it is already admin-scoped, not a generic/shared component. Pointing `templateName` at the corresponding admin template (`admin/templates/group_member`) is consistent with how the diff introduces that template file, and adding `classNames: ["item"]` is a normal way to hook styling for that view. The finding is an architectural/style critique (“leaking styling concerns”) rather than a verifiable bug/correctness/security defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Route/controller param mismatch: routes under resources :groups set params[:id] but admin/groups_controller.rb add_members and remove_member call params.require(:group_id), causing ActionController::ParameterMissing (400) on every real request, making member add/remove non-functional in production

adjudication.rationale: The diff’s routes are defined *inside* `resources :groups` as `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"`. In Rails this generates member-style nested paths like `/admin/groups/:group_id/members(.:format)`, which provide `params[:group_id]` (not `params[:id]`). This is also consistent with the client-side calls (`/admin/groups/" + id + "/members.json`) and the updated specs using `group_id:`. Therefore `params.require(:group_id)` in `add_members`/`remove_member` matches the route and will not raise `ParameterMissing` on normal requests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Tests never catch the param mismatch because controller specs inject group_id directly via xhr, bypassing routing entirely (green-tests/red-feature)

Public group members page silently truncated to 50 members with no pagination controls — limit is unconditionally applied server-side and the public group/members.hbs template has no next/previous UI, hiding members from end users

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff changes member fetching to always apply `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i`, and returns only that slice (`limit(limit).offset(offset)`) for *all* groups, not just automatic ones. On the client side, the public template `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` still just renders a table of `members` and the route `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6` only calls `model.findMembers()` without adding any pagination actions/UI. No next/previous controls (like the new admin group page has) are introduced for the public members page, so groups with >50 users will only show the first 50 with no way to navigate to the rest.

adjudication_records.issue_text: totalPages computed property in admin-group.js.es6 uses Math.floor(user_count/limit) + 1, producing an off-by-one phantom empty last page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit; should use Math.ceil

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 50 users, limit 50), this yields 2 pages instead of 1. The `next` action then allows navigating to `offset = user_count` (min(offset+limit, user_count)), and `findMembers()` requests `offset=50`, which the server will return as an empty members list—creating a phantom empty last page. Using `Math.ceil(user_count/limit)` (and/or clamping offset to `user_count - limit`) would avoid this off-by-one.

adjudication_records.issue_text: group_member.hbs remove link guards on `automatic` but the item template's context is the member (Discourse.User) which has no automatic property, so the guard evaluates falsy and the remove icon is shown on automatic groups, yielding 422 errors when clicked
add_members silently ignores unknown usernames and returns success_json, giving the admin zero feedback when no users are added (combined with the TODO to clear the input)

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only adds a user if `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user; unknown usernames are simply skipped with no error or response detail. After the loop it calls `group.save` and, if it succeeds, renders `success_json` regardless of whether any users were actually added. If all provided usernames are unknown, the request still returns success with no feedback that nothing changed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member executes group.users.delete(user_id) immediately (destroying the join row) before group.save, so if group.save fails afterward the controller reports an error even though the member was already removed, leaving stale UI

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#remove_member, the code calls `group.users.delete(user_id)` and only afterward checks `if group.save`. In Rails, `association.delete(...)` immediately persists the removal of the join row; it does not depend on `group.save`. Therefore, if `group.save` were to fail (e.g., validations/callbacks on Group), the controller would respond with an error even though the membership was already removed, creating a possible inconsistency between server state and reported result. This ordering/extra save is a real correctness risk introduced in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member spec uses xhr :put for a DELETE-routed action, exercising the action with the wrong HTTP verb because controller specs bypass routing, hiding the P1 param mismatch

adjudication.rationale: Real issue in the diff: `config/routes.rb` wires `remove_member` to a **DELETE** route (`delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`). But the new controller spec context for `.remove_member` calls it with `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...` (as shown at the end of the diff). In Rails controller specs, this will still invoke the action despite the verb mismatch (it bypasses routing), so the spec does not actually test the real HTTP contract and could pass while the actual routed endpoint would not accept PUT.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public members template binds `members` but the group-members route sets the model and calls findMembers() on the group model, so `members` may resolve to undefined if the controller is not an ObjectController, rendering an empty table

Stale-count race in pagination: next/findMembers clamp offsets against locally cached user_count with no request-sequencing guard, allowing offset == user_count and a permanently empty last page under concurrent mutations or out-of-order promise resolution
